acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Vampires family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Progenitor, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the First-Crest Blood Court Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: An inhumanly beautiful corpse-pale sovereign seated on a blood-glass throne, wearing a crown fine enough to seem grown, dressed in ageless black couture, and framed by three segmented wings of pure shadow aligned to crest vessels.

Signature mechanic: First Blood Court: three tall blood-glass vessels rise behind the throne beneath the grown-looking crown. The Hunt vessel marks wounds and sends Thralls that surviving Bloodkin can pull into circles; the Courtesy vessel appoints a Noble whose shattered crest opens a strike on the throne; the Salon vessel lets an Ancient divide the arena with cloak panels. The Progenitor spreads one pure-shadow wing toward the selected vessel and feeds it through a visible glass vein. Breaking that vein during the lower-form phase shatters the vessel, dismisses its command, and tears away the corresponding wing section. Once two vessels fall, the Progenitor leaves the throne, using only the remaining crest while each shadow-wing recovery exposes the crown root.
battlefieldDuty: Rule a three-crest blood-glass throne arena that stages Hunt, Courtesy, and Salon phases, promotes surviving lower Vampires, and sheds one shadow-wing command each time its lineage vessel breaks.
constructionDimensions: The T1 Thrall carries a cracked ceramic heat vessel at the shift knot and blackened claw caps; T2–T5 court materials become a night-forge system through heat-crazed blood-glass, charred velvet hems, ember vents in cane or clasp hardware, blackened membrane ribs, and heat-blued signets while corpse-white skin remains visible.

Predatory and ceremonial actions follow a heat cycle: blood-glass channels boil toward one limb, cloak vents open, smoke trails the committed lunge or command, and a cooled vessel or wing rib exposes recovery.
counterplay: Follow the selected crest, resolve or disrupt its familiar lower-form rule, then sever the visible throne vein while the wing is extended; every broken vessel removes a phase, a command route, and one protective wing section. Affinity signal: The active glass vessel clears and its gold fitting opens after a heated action; breaking the fitting vents the charge and interrupts the corresponding claw, cloak, or crest route.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only fire treatment without charred couture, vent hardware, and heat-cycled blood-glass
Glow-only fire treatment without a fuel vessel, heat route, or cooling joint
Flame skin that hides vampiric pallor, fangs, claws, posture, or tailoring
Generic burning blood with no distinction from family-native feeding matter
identityInvariants: A tall or lengthening human silhouette retains corpse-white skin, long fingers, fangs, claws, red eyes, and an absence of warm living complexion.
Posture escalates from feral hunch to impossible stillness; higher forms widen through fitted coats, tailored cloaks, bat membrane, or shadow wings without obscuring humanlike anatomy.
Black, bone pallor, deep blood red, and aged gold remain paired with velvet, silk, brocade, polished leather, blood-glass, and bat membrane.
Blood is family-native feeding matter and lineage symbolism rather than Fire or Water affinity by itself; every use has a source, route, vessel, or recoverable feeding window.
Signet rings, high collars, jeweled clasps, medals, canes, blades, and family crests communicate authored encounter rank while exposing the hand, vessel, or crest that carries each command.
telegraph: The impossibly still face turns toward one vessel, a fine crown branch aligns with its glass vein, the matching shadow wing unfolds, and every lower Vampire adopts that phase's learned posture.
